q: What is the main difference between a chatbot and an agent?
options: A chatbot can read files, an agent cannot
An agent loops — it plans, calls tools, observes results, and iterates to finish a goal
A chatbot is paid, an agent is free
An agent only answers one question then stops
explanation: A chatbot answers and stops. An agent works toward a goal by calling tools and iterating until the task is done.

q: "ChatGPT answers. An agent works." What does the phrase 'an agent works' mean in plain terms?
options: It applies for jobs on your behalf automatically
It performs multi-step tasks in your environment using tools, not just text replies
It writes all your essays for you
It charges for every single word it produces
explanation: An agent executes tasks end-to-end in your environment — searching, reading files, running code, sending messages — rather than just replying with text.

q: Which of these is NOT part of a personal agent's environment?
options: Files it can read and edit
A warranty from the app store
explanation: An agent's environment is made of the tools that let it act: files, code, the web, and messaging. A warranty is not part of that.

q: What makes an agent 'personal' rather than a generic chat tool?
options: It remembers you, your tools, and your context across sessions
It only works on one specific topic
It is physically installed in your phone
It never connects to the internet
explanation: A personal agent is tuned to your life: your email, calendar, research, and way of working. It remembers and holds the context that makes it useful to *you*.
